items.quote: Since hosting the 1988 Winter Olympics, the city has also been home to a number of major winter sporting facilities
items.note: Calgary has hosted the Winter Olympics once only, so the year is unique.

items.quote: The Calgary Stampede has continued as a civic tradition for over 100 years, marketing itself as the "greatest outdoor show on earth"
items.note: en:Calgary_Stampede also confirms it is held every July.

items.quote: Calgary is at the confluence of the Bow River and the Elbow River
items.note: Nose Creek also joins the Bow in the city, but it is a creek; the two rivers are unambiguous.

items.quote: the National Hockey League's Calgary Flames and Edmonton Oilers
the Canadian Football League's Calgary Stampeders and Edmonton Elks
YYC – the International Air Transport Association code for Calgary International Airport is used to refer to the city
items.note: The Calgary article's own nickname list omits YYC (it gives Cowtown, Stampede City), but the question specifies the airport code, so no other answer fits.

items.quote: Winters in Calgary are lengthy and cold, with wild and unpredictable temperature swings due to the chinook winds
items.note: en:Chinook_wind gives rises from below -20 C to as high as 10 C within hours, so '20 degrees' (Celsius, unstated) is conservative.

items.quote: It is loosely based on the debut of the Jamaican national bobsleigh team at the 1988 Winter Olympics
Calgary's light rail system, known as the CTrain, was the second light rail system in North America
Calgary is in southwestern Alberta and also next to the Rocky Mountains
items.note: 'The Canadian Rockies' or 'the Rockies' should also be accepted.
